entities.name: Polycystic ovary syndrome
observations: In women with PCOS, normal-weight participants with normal or excess abdominal adiposity failed to suppress MNC-derived TNF-alpha, IL-6, and IL-1beta after a 75-g oral glucose load.
The PCOS-associated cytokine response was concluded to be independent of excess adiposity, although adiposity and androgens correlated with response measures.

entities.name: PMID:25078146
observations: Ramezani Tehrani et al., JCEM 2014; studied 23 women with PCOS and 24 ovulatory controls stratified by weight and abdominal adiposity using DEXA.
Normal-weight controls suppressed MNC cytokine release after glucose; both normal-weight PCOS groups and obese participants failed to suppress it.
Authors concluded the altered PCOS response was not regulated by excess adiposity; obesity independently produced a similar response.

entities.name: PMID:24576416
observations: Weight-matched 2014 study of 16 PCOS women and 15 controls found lean PCOS and obese controls failed to suppress LPS-stimulated MNC IL-6 and IL-1beta after glucose, whereas obese PCOS suppressed both.
The authors interpreted the systemic response as independent of obesity; chronic inflammation and possible LPS tolerance may explain the obese-PCOS MNC pattern.

entities.name: PMID:15985479
observations: Earlier controlled study found weight-class differences in LPS-stimulated MNC TNF-alpha responses after glucose; lean PCOS had greater truncal fat than lean controls.
The study suggested abdominal adiposity contributes to inflammation and insulin resistance but did not establish that adiposity explains the PCOS-specific response.
